comments.content: Typo in doc comment: "returns returns" is duplicated, and "it's value" should be "its value".

The doc comment describes the curve as symmetric around `mean` over `[mean - width, mean + width]`, but the implementation only maps `x` back to `[0, width]` and calls `Smoothstep(x, 0, width)`. For the default (mean=0.5, width=0.5), an input outside [0, 1] (e.g. x < 0 or x > 1) produces `x` values outside [0, width], which Smoothstep will clamp — but the resulting behavior differs from a true bell curve for out-of-range inputs. Please confirm callers always pass x in [mean-width, mean+width] (here deltaDifferenceFraction is in [0,1), so it's fine), or document/clamp the domain explicitly to avoid misuse.

`reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio - (long)reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio` will throw an OverflowException (or produce undefined behavior) if `reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio` exceeds long.MaxValue, and more importantly can be negative/incorrect for very large ratios. While prevDelta/currDelta are unlikely to produce such extremes, consider using `reverseDeltaDifferenceRatio % 1.0` (or Math.Floor) instead of casting to long to make the fractional-part extraction robust and clearer in intent.
